summary:
CRITICAL ID CORRECTION: arXiv 1903.05168 is NOT the Jaques et al. paper — it is Lowe et al., "On the Pitfalls of Measuring Emergent Communication" (AAMAS 2019). The Jaques et al. "Social Influence" paper is arXiv 1810.08647 (ICML 2019, PMLR 97:3040–3049, best-paper honourable mention). I read both papers in full (PDFs saved locally from arXiv; all pages extracted).

== JAQUES ET AL. (arXiv 1810.08647, v4) ==
Setting: Markov game <S,T,A,r>, N=5 agents, partial observability (agent k sees egocentric view s_t^k, 15x15 window), A3C training, conv+FC+LSTM nets with internal LSTM state u_t^k. Environments: SSDs Cleanup (public goods) and Harvest (common-pool), from Leibo et al. 2017 / Hughes et al. 2018 (code: github.com/eugenevinitsky/sequential_social_dilemma_games).

(1) Causal influence reward. Immediate reward is modified to r_t^k = \alpha e_t^k + \beta c_t^k (e extrinsic, c influence). Agent j conditions its policy on k's action: p(a_t^j | a_t^k, s_t^j). k intervenes with counterfactuals \tilde a_t^k and computes j's marginal policy p(a_t^j|s_t^j) = \sum_{\tilde a_t^k} p(a_t^j | \tilde a_t^k, s_t^j) p(\tilde a_t^k | s_t^j) ("j's policy if it did not consider agent k"). Eq. (1): c_t^k = \sum_{j=0, j\neq k}^{N} D_{KL}\!\big[\, p(a_t^j\,|\,a_t^k, s_t^j) \,\big\|\, \sum_{\tilde a_t^k} p(a_t^j\,|\,\tilde a_t^k, s_t^j)\, p(\tilde a_t^k\,|\,s_t^j) \big] = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[\,p(a_t^j|a_t^k,s_t^j)\,\|\,p(a_t^j|s_t^j)\,]. They note KL can be replaced by other divergences (JSD, PMI) — reward is empirically robust to the choice. Basic model assumptions: centralized computation of c from j's policy, and unidirectional influence (disjoint influencer/influencee sets; influencers act first).

(2) Relation to MI (Supp. Sec. 10.1). With z_t = <u_t^j, s_t^j> the per-pair reward is D_{KL}[p(a_t^j|a_t^k,z_t) || p(a_t^j|z_t)] (Eq. 4). Identity (Eq. 5): I(A^j;A^k|z) = \sum_{a^k,a^j} p(a^j,a^k|z)\log\frac{p(a^j,a^k|z)}{p(a^j|z)p(a^k|z)} = \sum_{a^k} p(a^k|z)\, D_{KL}[p(a^j|a^k,z)\|p(a^j|z)] — i.e., the KL factor IS the influence reward, so sampling k's actions from p(a^k|z) over N trajectories gives a Monte-Carlo estimate (Eq. 6): I \approx \frac{1}{N}\sum_n D_{KL}[p(A^j|a_n^k,z)\|p(A^j|z)]. IMPORTANT: the paper claims the influence reward is, IN EXPECTATION, EXACTLY the conditional MI (unbiased MC estimator), not merely a lower bound — the prompt's "lower bound" framing is not how the paper states it. They train with Eq. 1 (per-action KL) rather than Eq. 5 because it gives the DIRECTED causal effect of the specific action taken, i.e., better credit assignment; whether the learned policy approximates MI depends on learning dynamics. They also frame influence as a social form of empowerment, and note it reduces policy-gradient variance (conditional variance <= marginalized variance). PMI alternative (Eq. 7): pmi(a^k;a^j|Z=z) = \log\frac{p(a^j|a^k,z)}{p(a^j|z)}, equivalent to Lizier & Prokopenko's "local information flow".

(3) Communication experiments (Sec. 5). Explicit cheap-talk channel a la Foerster et al. 2016: each agent emits a discrete symbol m_t^k; combined vector m_t = [m_t^0..m_t^N] is input to every agent at the next timestep. Architecture: extra A3C head with communication policy \pi_m and value V_m; the environment policy \pi_e, V_e are trained ONLY with environmental reward; \pi_m is trained with r = \alpha e + \beta c, where influence is over the previous-timestep message (Eq. 2): c_t^k = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[p(a_t^j | m_{t-1}^k, s_t^j) \| p(a_t^j | s_t^j)]. They argue message-influence cannot be manipulative: j is free to ignore messages, and \pi_e only shifts on messages containing environmentally useful information — so influential communication must be useful to the listener. In Cleanup, optimal \alpha = 0 (influence alone trains the comm head). Findings: influence-comm agents learn faster/higher collective reward; being-influenced correlates with individual environmental reward (Cleanup rho=.67, Harvest rho=.34, both p<0.001, over 100 conditions); influence is sparse in time (>mean influence in <10% of timesteps; listeners listen selectively). Honesty argument relies on repeated interactions (lying loses future influence) — not guaranteed one-shot.

(4) Metrics (partially inspired by Bogin et al. 2018): (a) Speaker consistency (normalized in [0,1], Supp Eq. 8): SC = \sum_{k=1}^N 0.5\big[\sum_c (1 - H(p(a^k|m^k=c))/H_{max}) + \sum_a (1 - H(p(m^k|a^k=a))/H_{max})\big], H_max = max entropy given #symbols/#actions; measures 1:1 action-message correspondence. (b) Instantaneous coordination, two MI variants: symbol/action IC = I(m_t^k; a_{t+1}^j) and action/action IC = I(a_t^k; a_{t+1}^j), averaged over all trajectory steps then max over agent pairs; explicitly "instantaneous" — cannot capture compositional/delayed influence. Baselines show ~zero IC (consistent with Crawford & Sobel cheap-talk theory); influence agents show high IC only at "influential moments" (timesteps with influence > mean).

(5) MOA and counterfactual computation (Secs. 6, 8). Model of Other Agents: second FC+LSTM branch on the shared conv encoder, trained with observed trajectories via cross-entropy to predict p(a_{t+1} | a_t, s_t^k). Each agent internally simulates counterfactual replacements of its own action, uses MOA to get p(a_{t+1}^j | \tilde a_t^k, s_t^k), marginalizes to get p(a_{t+1}^j|s_t^k), and computes its own influence reward — fully decentralized (no access to other agents' rewards or policies). Noise mitigation: reward only granted when influencee j is within k's field of view (side effect: proximity bias). Causal details (Sec. 8): this is counterfactual conditioning (no abduction needed since all inputs are observed/stored), not do-calculus average effects. Correct conditioning set must include the influencee's LSTM state: Eq. (3): c_t^k = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[p(a_t^j|a_t^k,s_t^j,u_t^j) \| p(a_t^j|s_t^j,u_t^j)]. Causal diagrams (Fig. 8): basic case has no backdoor from a_t^k to s_t (collider not conditioned); in the MOA cross-timestep case, backdoor through s_t is blocked by colliders at s_{t+1}, u_{t+1}^j; conditioning on s_t^k suffices but <u_t^k, s_t^k, a_t^k> are all MOA inputs; MOA must implicitly model the transition T and aspects of u_{t+1}^j. Results: influence-MOA beats A3C and MOA-as-auxiliary-task baselines; final collective rewards (Table 4): A3C 89/485 (Cleanup/Harvest), inequity aversion (Hughes) 275/750, influence-basic 190/1073, influence-comm 166/951, influence-MOA 392/588. Box-trapped sanity check: A3C opens the box in 0% of trajectories vs 88% for influence agent, with an influence-reward spike at box opening.

(6) Stated limitations: cooperative emergence may depend on environment/task specifics and on tuning the extrinsic/influence trade-off (alpha, beta); influence could in principle be non-cooperative; basic model needs centralized training and unidirectional influence (later relaxed); IC metrics are instantaneous only; MOA inaccuracy yields noisy rewards; visibility constraint biases toward proximity; honesty argument fails one-shot; curriculum (C in [0.2-3.5]x10^8 steps) can delay learning.

== LOWE ET AL. (arXiv 1903.05168, AAMAS 2019, pp. 693-701) ==
Framework: Markov games with actions split A_i = A_i^e \cup A_i^m (disjoint); messages are discrete, observed next step, don't affect dynamics, cost r_c = 0 (cheap talk). Two prerequisites for communication: (1) sender's signal relates to its observation/intended action -> POSITIVE SIGNALING; (2) receiver updates beliefs/behaviour -> POSITIVE LISTENING. Definition 3.1 (Positive Signaling): with \bar m = (m_0..m_T), \bar o, \bar a over a trajectory, an agent exhibits positive signaling iff \bar m \not\perp \bar o or \bar m \not\perp \bar a. Definition 3.2 (Positive Listening): exists a message m \in A_i^m from another agent s.t. ||\pi(o, \mathbf{0}) - \pi(o, m)||_\tau > 0, where \mathbf{0} is the zero vector and ||.||_\tau is a distance on expected trajectories under \pi. Metrics: SC = \sum_{a \in A^e}\sum_{m \in A^m} p(a,m)\log\frac{p(a,m)}{p(a)p(m)} with p(a,m) empirical co-occurrence of an agent's OWN (message, action) pairs over episodes (Jaques SC is a normalized version); IC = same formula with speaker's message and the OTHER agent's next action; Context Independence (Bogin et al.): m^c = \arg\max_m p_{cm}(c|m), CI = \frac{1}{|C|}\sum_c p_{mc}(m^c|c)\, p_{cm}(c|m^c) (needs a concept space; estimated with IBM Model 1); message entropy H(\pi^c); message input norm MIN = ||W_m^1|| (first-layer weights from message inputs; zero norm => no positive listening); Delta r = reward gain from adding a channel. CIC (causal influence of communication, Sec. 3.3, terminology adopted from concurrent Jaques et al.): interventional one-step MI — per test game, intervene on the speaker's message; p(m_j) = \pi_2(m_j|o_2), p(a|m_j) = \pi_1(a|o_1, m_j), p(a,m_j) = p(a|m_j)p(m_j), p(a) = \sum_m p(a,m), CIC += \frac{1}{T}\sum_{a\in A^e} p(a,m_j)\log\frac{p(a,m_j)}{p(a)p(m_j)}; crucially normalized WITHIN each game (not across games, unlike IC), and one must condition on all variables affecting the listener's action to block back-door paths (Pearl). Key experimental result (Matrix Communication Games, REINFORCE, randomized Gaussian payoffs N(0,3)): agents exhibit strong SC, CI, low message entropy — appearing communicative — yet CIC is at its minimum (messages causally inert): avg CIC 1.408/1.797/2.303 vs min 1.386/1.792/2.303 for 2x2/4x4/8x8 (min = ln M for vocab M=4/6/10); scrambling received messages leaves SC unchanged (e.g. 0.198 vs default 0.202 on 2x2). Cause: shared hidden layers between action and communication heads make representations linearly separable by intended action, so the linear comm head signals actions as a byproduct; a separate comm network kills SC (0.028); SC appears even with untrained comm parameters (lambda_c=0: 0.171-0.686). Probes show messages are redundant given the payoff matrix. Same pattern in iterated MCGs with A2C (5-round memory, gamma=0.9, n=5-step returns). Conclusion table: SC and CI are sufficient but NOT necessary for positive signaling and say nothing about listening; IC is sufficient but not necessary for positive listening (misses state-dependent listening — counterexample: truthful signaler + best-responding listener with random payoffs gives IC=0 because p(a,m) marginalizes over R); MIN is necessary but not sufficient for listening; Delta r is a strong overall indicator (sufficient for detecting communication, not necessary — conventions can substitute); CIC "should always be used". Recommendations: use interventional/causal metrics, don't just ablate the channel at test time (distribution-shift fragility — retrain with/without channel instead); scale CIC by sampling messages from the comm policy and measuring behaviour change over finite horizons for nearby agents; extend metrics compositionally/temporally (one-step CIC is a limitation); benchmark against multiple metrics to avoid metric exploitation.

Follow-up: Eccles et al. (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv 1912.05676) turn positive signaling and positive listening into explicit inductive-bias losses enabling decentralized emergent communication in temporally extended settings.

key_facts: arXiv ID correction: Jaques et al. 'Social Influence' = arXiv:1810.08647 (ICML 2019, PMLR 97:3040-3049); arXiv:1903.05168 = Lowe et al. 'On the Pitfalls of Measuring Emergent Communication' (AAMAS 2019, pp. 693-701).

Jaques Eq. 1 (basic influence): c_t^k = \sum_{j=0, j\neq k}^{N} D_{KL}[ p(a_t^j | a_t^k, s_t^j) \| \sum_{\tilde a_t^k} p(a_t^j | \tilde a_t^k, s_t^j) p(\tilde a_t^k | s_t^j) ] = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[ p(a_t^j|a_t^k,s_t^j) \| p(a_t^j|s_t^j) ]; total reward r_t^k = \alpha e_t^k + \beta c_t^k.

Jaques Eq. 2 (communication influence): c_t^k = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[ p(a_t^j | m_{t-1}^k, s_t^j) \| p(a_t^j | s_t^j) ] — influence of previous-timestep message m_{t-1}^k on listener's action; comm head \pi_m trained with r = \alpha e + \beta c while action head \pi_e uses only environmental reward; optimal \alpha=0 in Cleanup.

Jaques Eq. 3 (correct conditioning set): c_t^k = \sum_{j\neq k} D_{KL}[ p(a_t^j | a_t^k, s_t^j, u_t^j) \| p(a_t^j | s_t^j, u_t^j) ] — must condition on influencee's LSTM state u_t^j to remove cross-timestep dependencies (no abduction needed; counterfactual conditioning, not do-calculus).

MI claim (Supp 10.1, Eqs. 5-6): I(A^j;A^k|z) = \sum_{a^k} p(a^k|z) D_{KL}[p(a^j|a^k,z) \| p(a^j|z)] with z = <u_t^j, s_t^j>; sampled influence reward is an unbiased Monte-Carlo estimate: I \approx (1/N)\sum_n D_{KL}[p(A^j|a_n^k,z)\|p(A^j|z)] — 'in expectation, the social influence reward is the MI between agents' actions' (equality in expectation, NOT stated as a lower bound). Eq. 7: pmi(a^k;a^j|z) = log[p(a^j|a^k,z)/p(a^j|z)]; KL/PMI/JSD all work.
Jaques speaker consistency (Supp Eq. 8): SC = \sum_{k=1}^N 0.5[ \sum_c (1 - H(p(a^k|m^k=c))/H_{max}) + \sum_a (1 - H(p(m^k|a^k=a))/H_{max}) ], normalized in [0,1].

Jaques instantaneous coordination: symbol/action IC = I(m_t^k; a_{t+1}^j), action/action IC = I(a_t^k; a_{t+1}^j); averaged over trajectory steps then max over agent pairs; high IC for influence agents only at 'influential moments' (influence > mean, <10% of timesteps).

MOA: second FC+LSTM branch on shared conv encoder trained with cross-entropy to predict p(a_{t+1}|a_t, s_t^k); agent computes own influence reward from counterfactuals through its MOA; reward only given when influencee is within field of view; decentralized (no reward sharing or centralized controller).

Jaques results: influence/individual-reward correlation Cleanup rho=.67, Harvest rho=.34 (p<0.001); final collective reward (Cleanup/Harvest): A3C 89/485, inequity aversion 275/750, influence-basic 190/1073, influence-comm 166/951, influence-MOA 392/588; Box-trapped: open-box 0% (A3C) vs 88% (influence). Implementation: conv(kernel 3, stride 1, 6 ch), 2xFC(32), LSTM(128), gamma=.99, N=5 agents, curriculum C in [0.2-3.5]x10^8 steps; comm hyperparams Cleanup beta=2.752 alpha=0 vocab=9, Harvest beta=4.825 alpha=1.0 vocab=7; MOA beta=.620/2.521, MOA loss weight 15.007/10.911.
Lowe Def 3.1 (Positive Signaling): with \bar m=(m_0..m_T), \bar o, \bar a over a trajectory, positive signaling iff \bar m \not\perp \bar o or \bar m \not\perp \bar a (statistical dependence).

Lowe Def 3.2 (Positive Listening): exists message m \in A_i^m from another agent with ||\pi(o, \mathbf{0}) - \pi(o, m)||_\tau > 0, \mathbf{0} = zero vector, ||.||_\tau a distance on expected trajectories under \pi.

Lowe SC (Eq. 2): SC = \sum_{a\in A^e}\sum_{m\in A^m} p(a,m) log[p(a,m)/(p(a)p(m))], p(a,m)=(1/N)\sum_i 1_{act=a,comm=m} empirical co-occurrences across episodes; Jaques SC is a normalized version of this; IC uses the same formula with the OTHER agent's action.

Lowe context independence (from Bogin et al.): \forall c: m^c = argmax_m p_{cm}(c|m); CI(p_{cm},p_{mc}) = (1/|C|)\sum_c p_{mc}(m^c|c) \cdot p_{cm}(c|m^c); requires a concept space and IBM Model 1 estimation; punishes synonyms.

Lowe CIC (Algorithm 1, one-step): per test game, intervene on speaker's message: p(m_j)=\pi_2(m_j|o_2), p(a|m_j)=\pi_1(a|o_1,m_j), p(a,m_j)=p(a|m_j)p(m_j), p(a)=\sum_m p(a,m); CIC += (1/T)\sum_{a\in A^e} p(a,m_j) log[p(a,m_j)/(p(a)p(m_j))]; normalized within each game (unlike IC which averages across games); must condition on all variables affecting the listener's action to block back-door paths (Pearl).

Lowe headline result: in randomized-payoff MCGs (entries ~ N(0,3); sizes 2x2/4x4/8x8 with vocab M=4/6/10), SC/CI/entropy suggest communication but CIC is at minimum: avg 1.408+/-0.002, 1.797+/-0.001, 2.303+/-0.001 vs min 1.386, 1.792, 2.303 (= ln M); 89.3%/97.9%/99.9% of games have CIC < 1.02*min; scrambling received messages leaves SC unchanged (0.198 vs 0.202 on 2x2); separate comm network eliminates SC (0.028); SC persists with untrained comm head (lambda_c=0: 0.171).

Lowe mechanism: shared hidden layers between action and comm heads make last-layer representations linearly separable by intended action (PCA, Fig. 3), so the linear comm output spuriously encodes actions — positive signaling WITHOUT positive listening; IC counterexample: truthful signaler + payoff-dependent best-responding listener yields IC=0 in expectation because p(a,m) marginalizes over the random payoff R.

Lowe metric verdicts (Table 4): SC and CI sufficient but not necessary for positive signaling, neither indicates listening; H(pi^c) indicates neither; IC sufficient but not necessary for positive listening (misses state-dependent listening); MIN (=||W_m^1||, first-layer message-input weight norm) necessary but not sufficient for listening; Delta r a strong overall indicator; CIC 'should always be used to determine effect communication has on agent behaviour'.

Lowe code: github.com/facebookresearch/measuring-emergent-comm; MCG agents: REINFORCE, 2-layer feedforward, shared body with separate linear heads for action/comm/baseline, J(theta) = J_pol(theta^a) + lambda_c J_pol(theta^c) + lambda_ent(J_ent(theta^a)+J_ent(theta^c)) + lambda_v J_v(theta^v); iterated case: A2C, memory of previous 5 rounds, gamma=0.9, 5-step returns.

gaps_or_risks: The prompt asked for a proof that influence is a 'lower bound' on MI; the paper actually proves equality in expectation (the influence reward is an unbiased Monte-Carlo estimator of I(A^k;A^j|z) when k's actions are sampled from p(a^k|z)). It becomes a biased estimate once the policy is trained on the reward (sampling no longer matches the marginalizing distribution) — the paper flags this as 'depends on the learning dynamics' but gives no bound in either direction.

Two checkmark cells of Lowe et al. Table 4 (the Qual. row and the asterisk placement on Delta r / CIC positive-signaling columns) were read from a rendered page image and could be slightly misread; the confident entries (SC/CI/IC/MIN/CIC verdicts quoted above) match the surrounding prose.

Lowe et al.'s min-CIC values numerically equal ln(M) (1.386=ln4, 1.792=ln6, 2.303=ln10), implying their reported CIC includes a message-entropy floor rather than being 0 when messages are inert; the paper does not spell out this offset — verify against their code (github.com/facebookresearch/measuring-emergent-comm) before reimplementing.
Jaques et al. v4 PDF header still says 'Proceedings of the 35th ICML, Stockholm, PMLR 80, 2018' (a template artifact); the actual venue is ICML 2019, PMLR 97:3040-3049 — cite the latter.

Jaques et al.'s Table 1 basic-influence hyperparameters (number of influencers per environment) were partially hard to read from the rendered table; the values reported for beta, curriculum C, and divergence choice (JSD for Cleanup, PMI for Harvest in the basic experiment; KL in comm and MOA experiments) are reliable.

Both papers' communication analyses are one-step/instantaneous (message at t-1 -> action at t; one-step CIC): neither handles compositional or temporally extended influence — both explicitly list this as an open problem, relevant if the parent workflow's counterfactual EOD channel metrics need multi-step credit.

Jaques et al.'s counterfactual conditioning correctness depends on conditioning on the influencee's internal LSTM state u_t^j (Eq. 3); a reimplementation that conditions only on s_t^j reintroduces confounding through trajectory history.
